name: Help That Does Not Know The Person
problem: A general assistant answers from general knowledge. It does not know the person's quests, notes, decisions, past conversations, team or preferences, so its help is plausible but not theirs, and it can state things about their account that are not true.
who_has_it: Anyone asking AI about their own goals and work: Quest users in chat and teams with shared quests.
why_it_matters: Generic help has to be checked and corrected, which costs the time it was meant to save, and confident statements that do not rest on the person's own material erode trust.
why_hard: The relevant material is spread across many sources, far larger than any prompt, changes constantly, differs per person and team, and has to stay inside the scope it belongs to.
existing_attempts: Pasting context into a chat; custom assistants with uploaded files; retrieval products over a single document store; memory features in chat assistants.

name: Unreliable Help With The App
problem: Questions about how to use Quest, or what its AI can do for the person, are answered from guesses instead of the product's documentation and actual reach: the AI describes a capability it does not have, or says it cannot do something it can.
who_has_it: New users finding their way around the app, and team members who use only a fraction of its features.
why_it_matters: Guiding a person through the app is one of the AI's largest opportunities: a person who cannot find a feature does not use it, and a person told the AI cannot do something often stops asking. In production one person was told about a submission script that does not exist and two others were told AI work was switched off in their settings when the request could have been done.
why_hard: A usage question has to be told apart from a request to act; the documentation changes with every release; what the AI can reach differs per person, team and deployment, and a model fills a gap in its prompt with a plausible capability.
existing_attempts: The product documentation kept current and included in the chat's context; the message router; tool descriptions with when-to-use text; an answer check that flags claims of unexecuted work.

name: Lost Or Unreported Tasks
problem: Quest tasks attached to goals can be lost, run twice, or end without an outcome the person sees.
who_has_it: Quest users and teams who delegate research, drafting, checking and follow-up to AI, and the operators who run the worker.
why_it_matters: Delegated work that does not happen, or happens twice, stalls the goals it was meant to move, and people who cannot rely on it stop delegating.
why_hard: Several workers can poll the same queue and claims race, tasks have schedules and representatives, the worker can stop between claim and report, and a task has to be understood in the context of its goal.
existing_attempts: Doing the task by hand in a general chat assistant; scheduled scripts; a single worker; a database claim flag; manual re-queueing.

name: Different Answers On Different Surfaces
problem: The same request can get a different answer depending on the Quest surface it came from.
who_has_it: People who use Quest in chat, in scheduled tasks and in the apps, and the maintainers who keep each surface current.
why_it_matters: A person who gets two answers to one question cannot tell which to follow, and an improvement made for one surface does not reach the others.
why_hard: Each surface reaches Quest through its own path with its own data, timing and wording, and the differences are easy to add and hard to see.
existing_attempts: Separate handling per surface, and copying changes from one to another by hand.

name: Different Science Evidence In Two Chats
problem: One science question can get different evidence in Quest chat than in Quest's research chat.
who_has_it: People who ask science questions in Quest chat and in the research chat, and the maintainers who keep both current.
why_it_matters: Two searches mean two sets of sources and two ways of weighing them, so the same question can get different advice, and an improvement to one has to be made again in the other.
why_hard: The research chat's search belongs to the research interface and the evidence service behind the Quest backend, QAR reaches a host's research sources only through declared interfaces, and a host's research search reaches a run only as a retrieval source or a custom tool.
existing_attempts: Web research that reads snippets and then pages, with an answer check that flags claims the turn's reads do not support; a host's research search offered to a run as a retrieval source or a custom tool.
